newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end up but electronics erode gains.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end up but electronics erode gains.

text.p: Despite slippage by electronics, Taiwan share prices closed slightly higher on Tuesday as market liquidity flowed to big-capital shares tipped for inclusion in the island's debut warrants, brokers said.
The index closed up 25.52 points or 0.30 percent at 8,392.98, off an intra-day high of 8,419.90.
Turnover was an active T$138 billion.

Brokers said Taiwan's trendsetting sector, electronics, had slipped into a new correction against recent gains, easing 1.31 percent. Yet even as electronics cooled, warrant-eligible shares -- most of them blue-chip industrials -- drew buying interest.

Among the warrant-eligible, Textile giant Hualon topped list of the most actively traded issue, up T$2.3 or 6.95 percent to T$35.4. Another, food giant President Enterprises, was up T$2.5 or 4.81 percent to T$54.5.
"Investors are still very bullish about the market's outlook," said Taiwan Securities Investment analyst Joe Chiou.
"Most people agree that electronics should take a break for the moment, so they put their money in other blue chip stocks."
Computer maker Inventec Corp plunged T$13 or 6.88 percent to T$176 after saying it would lower its 1997 pre-tax profit forecast due to slowing orders for notebook computers.
"Inventec's decline triggers worries that other notebook computer makers might have been too optimistic," Foremost Investment's analyst Wang Jieh said.
Semiconductor makers Mosel was down T$2 to T$75.5, but United Microelectronics rebounded slightly from early decline to rise 50 cents at T$89.5 in late trade.
Brokers said they expected electronics to continue to lead the market after a short-term correction.
"Most people feel the correction on electronics will only be temporary," Tsao Chung-ping of Ting Kong Securities. "It will slow, but not upset, the market's firming trend."
